description: This file defines a custom exception class `DomainError` for representing domain-specific errors, along with factory functions to create standardized error instances such as not found, conflict, forbidden, and unauthorized errors. It is part of the core error handling mechanism in a Python project.

classes.name: DomainError
classes.description: An immutable, typed exception class for representing standardized domain errors with fields for code, message, HTTP status, and optional details.

methods.name: DomainError not_found(entity: str, entity_id: str)
methods.description: Creates a DomainError indicating that an entity with a given ID was not found.

methods.name: DomainError conflict(code: str, message: str, details: dict[str, Any] | None = None)
methods.description: Creates a DomainError indicating that a conflict occurred with provided details.

methods.name: DomainError forbidden(code: str, message: str)
methods.description: Creates a DomainError indicating a forbidden operation.

methods.name: DomainError unauthorized(message: str = "Unauthorized")
methods.description: Creates a DomainError indicating an unauthorized access.

ctags.name: conflict
ctags.pattern: /^def conflict(code: str, message: str, details: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> DomainError:$/
ctags.signature: (code: str, message: str, details: dict[str, Any] | None = None)
